newsitem.title: TURKEY: Power-short Turkey in big energy drive.
newsitem.headline: Power-short Turkey in big energy drive.

text.p: Turkey, which has started importing electricity to close energy deficits, plans to get more energy from nuclear, thermal and hydraulic plants and imported natural gas, officials said on Wednesday.
Ugur Dogan, undersecretary for the energy ministry, said the ministry would invite international bidders for a pipeline tender under a $23-billion 23-year natural gas deal struck with Iran in August.

"The tender will be opened in November. The project will cost about $1 billion," said Ugur Dogan, undersecretary for the energy ministry. "The Iranian gas agreement is going ahead as planned," he told Reuters.
The pipeline will carry an initial three billion cubic metres of Iranian natural gas annually from 1999, to be raised to 10 billion cubic metres from 2005.

Iran and Turkey each have to build the section of the pipeline through their territories to avoid breaching a U.S. decision in August that investors putting at least $40 million in energy projects in Iran and Libya would be punished.
Under the agreement Iran will have sold Turkey about 190 billion cubic metres of gas, to be mainly used for power generation along the line.
Dogan said the ministry would open another tender by mid-November for Turkey's first nuclear plant that will have a capacity of 700 to 1,100 MegaWatts (MW).

He said the nuclear plant's tender terms were prepared after consultations with the South Korean Atomic Energy Research Institute. "We will put the final touches to the tender terms and go out to the tender in early November, likely by mid-November."

The plant, planned for the Akkuyu region near the southern port of Mersin, would be financed entirely by the builders, according to the terms. Analysts say the plant, expected to produce about 11 billion kiloWatt-hours annually, might cost about $3 billion and will take about eight years to complete.

Turkey, whose energy demand is expected to rise 12 percent from a year earlier compared with a previous target of eight percent, said last month it would open another tender for a $2-billion thermal power plant in the east of the country that would produce two billion kiloWatt-hours (kWh) a year.

It will also sign a agreement with Russia, which sells it about six billion cubic metres of gas a year through a pipeline, to get up to 16 billion cubic metres of more gas through a $1.1 billion pipeline to be built via eastern Turkey.
The government announced last month tenders for 11 small-size hydraulic power plants that are expected to produce 9.29 billion kWh annually, and will tender for 44 more next year.
The energy ministry has been assessing bids for several gas and hydraulic power plants to be built by international energy companies. Officials said such projects will cost $6 billion.
Turkey has a power generation capacity of 105 billion kWh but expects to produce 93.1 billion kWh against a consumption expected at 97.5 billion kWh.
It has been in talks with Georgia and Bulgaria to import electricity from early 1997.
